text: Modelled against housing built in its place, Guangzhou’s Haizhu wetland keeps the area within 600 m about 0.25 °C cooler on a typical summer day, and over 1 °C cooler on the site itself. Without it, productivity in nearby heavy outdoor work would fall by 2.5% in May and 16.1% in October, monthly risk of death would rise by 1.23–1.27% from June to September, and cooling bills would rise by about US$1.9 million over 30 years.
lesson: Most of the wetland’s US$146.8 million value comes from carbon and mental health, not cooling. So make the heat case in lives, heavy outdoor work and bills, not money alone. And the same cooling is worth most to people without air conditioning.
how: Heavy outdoor work: hours and output kept in the heat
Health: change in heat deaths and illness
Who gains: households without air conditioning first
